justified.text: Rounding to the nearest multiple of a unit moves a value by at most half that unit, so the true value lies within the half-width of the printed one.

assumptions: The flood sheets are drawn in the UTM zone whose central meridian is `CENTRAL_MERIDIAN`, and their north arrow shows that grid's north.

No step of the placement models any rotation, so the whole convergence is left out. This holds in code: the control-point fit, the world-file export, the bundle adjustment and floodgap's pixel mapping are all translation and scale only.
The spherical convergence formula is accurate enough at the sheets' latitude, and one angle at the centre serves for the whole sheet.
The displacement at the corner, the largest anywhere on the sheet, is a fair measure of the omission's size.
The error figures in _georef.json are comparable from sheet to sheet, and describe the placement in use now.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read: export_flood.py changed only in write_readme() and a new helper for it; main(), which writes the manifest, is identical to the committed version, and docs/data/flood2012/manifest.json has the same hash; floodmaps.py changed only in a comment, with an identical syntax tree. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: Nothing in the repo establishes which grid the sheets were drawn in. The UTM premise rests on the docstring. The empirical check in `scripts/convergence.py:20` verifies UTM's own geometry, not that the sheets use UTM, and the sheet text read by floodmaps.py carries no projection statement. A grid with a different central meridian would give a different convergence.

The one independent test of the rotation, the terrain check, did not detect it beyond scatter (`scripts/convergence.py:37`). That result is recorded only in the docstring; `data/derived/terraincheck.json` holds no rotated run.

The denominator mixes two statistics. On control-point sheets it is `standard_error_m`; on automatically placed sheets it is `spread_m`, which the code itself calls small by construction, conditioned on the agreement it is meant to test (`scripts/floodmaps.py:430`). The site states that those figures were agreement between detectors and never accuracy (`docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md:227`). Ratios on those sheets, including the one that sets `shift_over_error_max`, are inflated against any true error.

The stated errors predate the bundle adjustment, which moved every automatically placed sheet much further than its `spread_m` (`docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md:227`). The current placement's accuracy as the export describes it, pair residuals plus control-point standard errors (`scripts/export_flood.py:160`, now computed from the registration records), is not what the ratio uses.

No code in scripts/ writes `standard_error_m` for the control-point sheets; the figures sit in _georef.json as hand-entered records. Each is a standard error of a fitted position, smaller than the scatter of the individual control points recorded beside it (`control_point_scatter_rms_m`). That scatter is where an unmodelled rotation would show, and nothing tests whether it does.
The ratio divides a maximum, the corner displacement, by a typical error. A like-for-like comparison would use the displacement at the control points or averaged over the sheet.

The convergence varies little between sheets (from `gamma_min_deg` to `gamma_max_deg`), so neighbouring sheets are rotated almost equally. The sheet-to-sheet consistency the bundle adjustment reports therefore cannot detect this rotation; only absolute anchors can.

In the docstring's worked check, the quoted drift and walk length give a bearing slightly smaller than the one stated (`scripts/convergence.py:20`). The discrepancy is small, but the check is not reproduced by any code.

The latitude constant `M_PER_DEG_LAT` differs from the one floodreg.py used to write the sheet bounds (`scripts/floodreg.py:34`), so ground half-diagonals are slightly understated. The effect is negligible, but the constants are inconsistent across scripts.

justified.text: The convergence formula is implemented in a few lines and evaluated at each sheet's own centre, as read from the world file currently served.
The placement really has no rotation term. The control-point fit solves longitude from pixel x and latitude from pixel y separately, and states that every sheet has north up.
The exported world files are written with both rotation terms set to zero, and every current world file carries none.
The bundle adjustment that later moved every sheet solves an east shift and a north shift per sheet, and no angle.
The corner displacement is the half-diagonal times the angle, a direct geometric consequence of turning a rectangle about its centre.
The script's docstring reports checking the angle empirically, by walking along a line of constant UTM easting and measuring the eastward drift.

Applying the rotation was tried and did not improve the independent terrain check beyond the scatter between sheets. The site therefore presents these numbers as the size of an omission, not as a correction.
The site describes this as the pipeline's own north-up statement set against the convergence it omits.

K-CONVERGENCE.licenses: A claim about the data pipeline: if the sheets are drawn in the assumed UTM grid, placing them north-up leaves out a rotation whose effect at the sheet corners is of the size given here. The registration error figures the pipeline records per sheet therefore do not bound the true placement error.
K-CONVERGENCE.model: For each world file in `docs/data/flood2012` with no rotation terms, the script takes the sheet-centre longitude and latitude from the world file and raster size. It computes $\gamma = \arctan\bigl(\tan(\lambda - \lambda_0)\,\sin\varphi\bigr)$, with $\lambda_0$ the zone's central meridian (in the code `gamma = atan(tan(lon - CENTRAL_MERIDIAN) * sin(lat))`), the transverse-Mercator convergence on a sphere. It converts the world file's pixel sizes to ground metres with `M_PER_DEG_LON * cos(lat)` and `M_PER_DEG_LAT`, and takes the corner displacement as the ground half-diagonal times `|gamma|` in radians, the arc a corner travels when the sheet turns about its centre. Each sheet's stated error is `standard_error_m`, or failing that `spread_m`, from `data/derived/floodmaps/_georef.json`. Their ratio is rounded, and the file reports the minimum and maximum of each quantity across sheets. The record is written on every run. Run with `--dry-run` the world files are untouched; run without it, they are also rewritten with the rotation applied.
K-CONVERGENCE.not_licensed: Anything about flooding, water or the city. It does not show that any sheet is actually misplaced by this amount: the grid is assumed, and the one independent test did not detect the rotation. It is not a correction to apply to the current placement, and it is not a calibrated accuracy ratio, least of all on the automatically placed sheets, whose denominator is detector agreement.
K-CONVERGENCE.title: Unmodelled grid-north rotation of the flood sheets
void_if: The sheets turn out to be drawn in a grid whose central meridian is not `CENTRAL_MERIDIAN`, or their north arrow shows true north.
Any placement step gains a rotation term. The convergence would then no longer be omitted, and these numbers would describe a pipeline that no longer exists.

The script is run without `--dry-run`. The world files are then rotated, a later run skips every sheet (`scripts/convergence.py:76`), and the record cannot be rebuilt until export_flood.py rewrites the world files.
The error fields in _georef.json are replaced or change meaning, for example by a re-registration that records a post-adjustment error.
The world files in `docs/data/flood2012` fall out of step with _georef.json. build.json lists the export manifest as this script's input, not the world files and rasters it actually reads.
K-CONVERGENCE.what: For each flood sheet, computes the meridian convergence at the sheet's centre, on the assumption that the sheet is drawn in a UTM grid, and the corner displacement that angle causes when the sheet is placed true-north-up, as every placement in this pipeline does. It then sets that displacement against the registration error the pipeline records for the sheet.

assumptions: The publisher's `typologi` value correctly says where water runs along each feature, on the surface or in a pipe.
The three named typologies all carry water on the surface where a person could see it, Forsinkelsesveje (retention roads, which hold water back) included.
No two features trace the same stretch of ground, so summing feature lengths does not count one alignment twice.
The layer's coordinates are geographic degrees, not a projected grid.
A flat-earth approximation with a cosine-of-latitude correction and fixed km-per-degree constants is accurate enough over the extent of one city.
The layer's geometry is the plan's alignment. It says nothing about whether an alignment has been built.

confirmed.by: fork w2-cs (re-read solutions.py: compute() and every constant it uses are identical to the version last read, checked by comparing their syntax trees; only page() changed - rewritten for checked claims - and the unused commit constant was replaced by the path to outfalls.json. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: No source cited anywhere in the repo defines the typologies. The mapping of Skybrudsveje, Grønne veje and Forsinkelsesveje to surface, and of Skybrudsledning to pipe, rests only on the script's own gloss (`scripts/conveyance.py:16`). Nothing argues that a retention road conveys water rather than holding it, or that a cloudburst road has no pipe beneath it.
Nothing checks for features that overlap or duplicate one another. A pipe drawn beneath a cloudburst road, or a segment digitised twice, would be summed twice into `total_km`.

The docstring's claim that the length formula is accurate to well under a percent is asserted, not tested. No code compares these lengths with an ellipsoidal or projected measurement, and the km-per-degree constants are fixed spherical values.

Sibling scripts use a different class definition. `rivermap.py` and `rivers3d.py` count 'mix' as surface (`scripts/rivermap.py:39`, `scripts/rivers3d.py:34`), while `surface_km` does not. rivermap.py's own docstring lists the surface set without 'mix' (`scripts/rivermap.py:16`), so that docstring and its code disagree.

A feature with an empty `typologi` becomes 'ukendt' and lands in `total_km` and `unclassified_km` without appearing in any provenance exclusion (`scripts/conveyance.py:71`). None occur in the current layer, but nothing guards against it.

The layer carries an expected in-service year, `forventet_ibrugtagning`, but this script ignores it. Every figure therefore mixes built, started and merely planned alignments (`docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md:353`).

justified.text: The typology split uses an attribute the publisher attaches to every feature. It is not a classification this project invented.
The class sets are fixed in code and applied mechanically to every feature, and features with no line geometry are counted rather than silently dropped.
The length formula is a few lines of visible arithmetic on the layer's own vertices, with no smoothing or resampling.

The class definition, the counts and the value under each alternative definition are written by the code that did the counting, so a reader can see that the number depends on which typologies are grouped as surface.
The conflicting figures this site once printed for this quantity are each reproduced by one of the recorded definitions. The disagreement was about definitions, not measurement.
The script names classification, not geometry, as the limiting error.

K-CONVEYANCE.licenses: Claims about what the published cloudburst plan layer contains: how much alignment it draws under each of its own typology labels, and how the surface-to-pipe comparison changes with the definition of surface. It also supports the conclusion that the site's earlier conflicting figures differed in definition, not in measurement.
K-CONVEYANCE.model: Each feature's `typologi` is read as its class. Surface is Skybrudsveje, Grønne veje and Forsinkelsesveje; pipe is Skybrudsledning; anything else (in practice only 'mix') is unclassified. For every feature with LineString or MultiLineString geometry, the script sums segment lengths computed on geographic longitude/latitude coordinates with a local flat-earth approximation, $\sqrt{(k_\lambda\,\Delta\lambda\,\cos\varphi)^2 + (k_\varphi\,\Delta\varphi)^2}$ - $\Delta\lambda$ and $\Delta\varphi$ the segment's steps in longitude and latitude, $k_\lambda$ and $k_\varphi$ the km-per-degree constants, $\varphi$ the latitude (in the code `hypot(dlon * km_per_deg_lon * cos(lat), dlat * km_per_deg_lat)`). The constants are fixed spherical values written inline, and $\varphi$ is taken at the segment's first point. Lengths are summed per typology, and the class totals are sums of those. Features with no line geometry are counted and dropped. Each headline figure is written together with a provenance block giving its class, its counts in and used, its exclusions, and the value under the other defensible class definitions.
K-CONVEYANCE.not_licensed: How much of the plan is built or in service; how much water any alignment can carry; whether water on a given alignment is actually visible; which part of a 'mix' alignment is surface. Nor does it support any statement about flooding, overflows or water quality, or comparison with other scripts' 'surface route' figures, which count 'mix' as surface.
K-CONVEYANCE.title: Cloudburst plan alignment length by typology
void_if: The layer is re-fetched and its `typologi` vocabulary changes. A new or renamed value would fall into `total_km` and `unclassified_km`, match neither class, have no exclusion reason, and stop `mix_km` equalling the unclassified length.
The layer's coordinates arrive in a projected grid rather than geographic degrees. Some Danish layers are published that way (`scripts/formats.py:113`), and the formula would then return nonsense.
Features in the layer are found to overlap or duplicate one another.
The publisher's `typologi` values turn out to encode something other than where the water runs, such as a funding programme or a project phase.
The layer is replaced by a different edition of the plan.
K-CONVEYANCE.what: Measures the length of every alignment in the city's cloudburst roads-and-pipes layer and splits it by the layer's own `typologi` attribute: water carried on the surface, in a pipe, or on a 'mix' alignment the layer does not break down.

assumptions: `Startklok` is the moment the bottle was filled, not the start of a cruise, the arrival at a station, or a default value.
The station's registered position, taken from the first row seen for it, is where every sample at that station was taken. The per-sample coordinates (`PrøveX_UTM32`, `PrøveY_UTM32`) are ignored.

The geometric elevation of the sun's centre is close enough to the apparent elevation for class assignment. Near the zero and minus-six boundaries, refraction and the solar disc's size can move a sample between classes.
A `Blandingsprøve` refers to a single depth and can stand as a point sample.
Rows are distinct measurements: there is no deduplication of replicate rows or of the same bottle reported twice.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read: the sample-type reading it cited from DATA_SOURCES.md was retired there, since the technical instruction does not define a Blandingsprøve; checked the pinned field-sampling chapter myself - its mixing passage is about nutrient, chlorophyll and primary-production subsamples - and recorded the reading as an inference in gaps. cycles.py changed only in that comment, verified by hash. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: The clock conventions are measured at summer-time changes; before summer time existed a convention cannot be seen, and those samples are excluded unless they are known defaults, which are excluded too.

The boundaries at zero and minus six degrees are stipulated. Nothing in the code or docs cites the civil-twilight convention they follow. Because the elevation is geometric and taken at the sun's centre, the zero boundary is not the published sunrise or sunset.

Some exclusions are silent: an unparseable clock, a malformed date, an unparseable depth or result, or a station without a usable position drops the row without being counted. This is unlike the type, censoring, unit and range exclusions, which are counted.
A station's position is cached from the first row seen for it. A bad coordinate on that row drops the station's samples for the whole run, without a count.

The total number of samples in each sun class is never written out; only the neighbour-conditioned counts per window are. A claim that divides the smallest window's night or twilight count by `results.o2.n` therefore compares two different populations and understates the dark-hour share.
The night and twilight classes do not separate pre-dawn from post-dusk. Nothing in the output supports reading them as pre-dawn counts.

The word `Blandingsprøve` is in none of the pinned chapters of the technical instruction, and the mixing passage concerns nutrient, chlorophyll and primary-production subsamples, not oxygen. That ODA's `Blandingsprøve` rows are pools at one depth is therefore an inference. They are a small minority of the surface oxygen rows; the count was made once and is not stored.

justified.text: The class boundaries are exactly `e < -6` for night and `e < 0` for twilight.
Sun elevation comes from the NOAA solar-position algorithm, which the script's author states is far more accurate than the degree-level precision the classes need.
The elevation is computed from the date, the time and the station's longitude and latitude, with no atmospheric refraction term.
The unit is checked on every row, because several parameters in this extract appear under more than one unit.

Only single-bottle and same-depth pooled samples are kept, following the technical instruction for Danish marine monitoring; depth-integrated samples are excluded because an integral is not a measurement at its midpoint.
Censored rows are dropped and counted, because `<` means the result field holds the detection limit, not a measurement.
The oxygen range is a physical plausibility filter, reasoned from solubility in cold fresh water.
The neighbour window is inclusive on both sides and excludes the sample itself; a sample with no neighbour is skipped.
`results.o2.n` is the number of oxygen samples retained before any window is applied.
Instants come from one function, with conventions measured per supplier and era rather than assumed for the whole archive.

The technical instruction's field-sampling chapter says that where one water depth is represented by water from several samplers, the water is mixed before subsampling for nutrients, chlorophyll and primary production: a pool at one depth, which is how a `Blandingsprøve` is read here.

K-CYCLES.licenses: Statements about when the monitoring programme sampled: how many archived surface oxygen bottle measurements pass the stated filters, and how few of them, under the Danish wall-clock reading of `Startklok`, were timed with the sun below the horizon and had a same-station neighbour within the window. This supports the claim that the archive barely observes surface oxygen in the dark hours. It is a finding about the sampling, not about the sea.
K-CYCLES.model: Each qualifying row's `Startklok` is parsed as hours and minutes. Each row's instant comes from `clock.instant()`, which applies the clock convention `scripts/clockzone.py` measured for the row's supplier and era and excludes filled-in defaults and mixed conventions. The station position is converted from the `X_UTM32` and `Y_UTM32` of the first row seen for that station and cached. `solar_elevation` (the NOAA algorithm, written out) gives the geometric elevation of the sun's centre, with no refraction correction. `sun_bin` maps `e < -6` to `night`, `-6 <= e < 0` to `twilight`, and bands above the horizon to the remaining classes. `results.o2.n` is the length of the retained oxygen list. For each window `W` in `WINDOWS`, `deviations` sorts each station's samples by date and counts a sample in its class only if the count of other samples with dates inside the inclusive plus-or-minus `W` day range is at least one.
K-CYCLES.not_licensed: Anything about oxygen concentrations at night, or the value of the pre-dawn minimum. A count of visits, stations or independent observations. The total number of night or twilight samples, since each window count excludes samples without a neighbour. A split between pre-dawn and post-dusk sampling. Anything below `MAX_DEPTH`, or from the CTD sonde record, which has no clock.
K-CYCLES.title: Surface oxygen samples placed by sun elevation

K-CYCLES.what: For surface oxygen, saturation and chlorophyll bottle samples, the script computes each sample's deviation from the mean of its own station's other samples within a moving window. The covered fields are the sample counts behind that: all retained oxygen samples, and those in the two below-horizon sun classes that had a same-station neighbour.

assumptions: A real diurnal cycle, if there is one, has the shape of the sun's elevation: flat at night, rising and falling with the sun. A cycle of another shape or phase would be recovered differently.
Everything the signal leaves out - season, site, weather, real variability - behaves within a window like independent Gaussian noise of the measured size.
Samples the clock cannot place are left out; the schedule tested is the schedule of the samples that can be placed.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read: cycles.py changed only in the comment on sample types, now saying the technical instruction does not settle what a Blandingsprøve is; no code changed, verified by hashing the file with that change undone. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: The sine-of-elevation shape is argued from how photosynthesis works, not fitted to observed diurnal oxygen curves in Danish water.

The simulated noise is Gaussian and independent. Real residuals may be heavier-tailed or correlated within a station, which would widen the real spread's distribution beyond the simulated one and make the bound too tight.
The thickness rule for bins, `MIN_BIN_N` in the script, is stipulated. Another rule changes the observed spread and every recovery together, but the bound may move.
The share of draws that reach the observed spread is itself estimated from a finite number of draws.

justified.text: Recovering a stipulated truth through the real observing system is an Observing System Simulation Experiment, the standard way meteorology and oceanography decide what an observing system can see.
The same logic applied to ocean observing networks.

Both sides are measured by the same code: the samples come from `cycles.read_samples()` and every spread, real or synthetic, from `cycles.deviations()` with the same window, bins and thickness rule. Nothing is re-implemented or typed in.
The schedule is not modelled: every sample's station, date, instant and position is the archive's own, placed in time by conventions measured at every summer-time change rather than assumed.

The noise is measured rather than assumed, where a diurnal signal cannot reach it: from samples whose window neighbours all share their sun bin, scaled for the size of the mean each residual is taken from.
Every amplitude is run on many draws, and draw by draw the amplitudes share a seed, so within a draw they differ by the signal alone; the bound and the null are shares of draws, not single outcomes.

K-DETECTABLE.licenses: What this sampling schedule and this estimator could and could not have detected, for a signal of this shape; and how often noise alone produces the spread the archive shows. Statements about the instrument.
K-DETECTABLE.model: Each synthetic value is a constant plus $A\,\bigl(\max(0,\ \sin e) - \tfrac{1}{2}\bigr)$, with $A$ the imposed amplitude and $e$ the sun's elevation (in the code `amp * (max(0, sin(elevation)) - 0.5)`), plus Gaussian noise with standard deviation `noise_sd_mg_l`, at the sun elevation of the sample's own instant (from `scripts/clock.py`) and place. `cycles.deviations()` turns every value into its deviation from the mean of its station's other samples inside the window, averages the deviations per sun bin, and the spread is the largest bin mean minus the smallest over the bins thick enough to count. The same function measures the real samples. Each amplitude is run on many draws; the bound is the smallest amplitude reaching the observed spread in at least `level` of them, and the draws at zero amplitude give the null.
K-DETECTABLE.not_licensed: Anything about the size of the real diurnal cycle on its own. Combined with the observed spread it yields only a conditional upper limit, never a value, and never a limit for a cycle of another shape.
K-DETECTABLE.title: Synthetic recovery on the real sampling schedule, over many noise draws
void_if: the real cycle's shape or phase differs strongly from the sun's elevation
the within-window noise is far from Gaussian, or depends on the hour
the clock conventions measured by `scripts/clockzone.py` are wrong for a supplier
K-DETECTABLE.what: Imposes a diurnal oxygen cycle of stipulated amplitude on the real instants and positions of the archive's surface samples, adds noise measured from the archive, and measures the result with the estimator the real data are measured with - over many noise draws per amplitude, once at the real times of day and once with the times redrawn.

assumptions: The series' month index counts months from January of `year0`, so its remainder modulo twelve is the calendar month.

An observation is one station-month of the series, which holds a monthly median per station: repeated casts within a month count once. On the nine-variable basis a station-month counts once for each variable, a reading of the convention chosen because under it, and not with the months merged across variables, the counts the brief first printed come out the same.

K-EA-BRIEF-SEASONAL.licenses: How many stations of the series fall in each class under this convention, and how the raw-R rule without a minimum behaves on `oxy_bed`.
K-EA-BRIEF-SEASONAL.model: Each station-month in `stations_series.bin` becomes a unit vector at the angle of its calendar month, $\theta = 2\pi m / 12$ with `m = month_index % 12`. For a station with N vectors, $R = |\sum_k e^{i\theta_k}| / N$ and $Z = N R^2$; the mean direction is the angle of the sum, rounded to the nearest month. Seasonal: `z > z_cut` and the mean month in June to September; year-round: `z <= z_cut` and `n >= min_n`; neither otherwise (`classify()` in `scripts/pages/agent_brief.py`). The raw-R group is `r > raw_r_cut` with no minimum.
K-EA-BRIEF-SEASONAL.not_licensed: Anything about the seasonality of the sea: the class describes when a station was observed, not what it observed.

assumptions: One `csv` record corresponds to one row of the source table. This holds for the CTD extract, where a full-file scan found no malformed rows. It fails in the water-chemistry extract wherever a free-text `Kvalitetsnote` contains quotation marks and line breaks that split it into extra one-field records.
The file on disk is the extract the numbers are meant to describe; the counts are of the fetched file, not of ODA's database, whose station list depends on the period requested.
The earlier version of the script that wrote the `ctd` entry counted records the same way the current code does.

confirmed.by: Claude research agent, main findings checked against the code by Claude (2026-09-10); not yet read by the project owner

gaps: The format declaration says records whose field count differs from the header must be skipped, but the script does not skip them. `kemi.rows` therefore includes note fragments that are not measurements.

The difference `kemi.rows - kemi.nonblank.Startklok` is used elsewhere as the number of rows without a clock time. It is the number of note fragments: every genuine row of the extract carries a `Startklok` value.
Non-blank does not mean valid. Nothing checks that a `Startklok` value parses as a time, which time zone it is in, or whether a value such as midnight is a placeholder.
The `ctd` entry was written by an earlier version of the script and carried forward by the merge. Nothing in the file records when it was made or from which copy of the extract.
The script is not registered in `data/manual/build.json`, so nothing marks these counts stale when an extract is re-fetched.

justified.text: A record is counted once for every row the reader yields, with no filter before the increment.
A value counts as non-blank only if its column is named, the field exists in the record, and it is non-empty after `strip()`.
The reader follows the declared ODA format: semicolon delimiter, `latin-1` encoding, double-quoted fields.
The CTD record count matches the independent full-file scan recorded in the format declarations, which found no malformed rows in that extract.

In `kemi.nonblank`, every column after the first has exactly the same count as `Startklok`, while the first column has more. So the records lacking a clock lack every field but the first, which is the pattern of the column-count trap the format declaration names. A streaming check made for this declaration confirmed that each such record has a single field of note text.
The CTD extract's own column list, as recorded by this script, has a `Dato` column and no clock column, which supports reading `ctd.rows` as readings that carry a date and no hour.
Merging rather than overwriting is deliberate, so that a run on one extract does not erase another's entry.

K-ENUMS.licenses: Statements about the extracts as held: how many records each contains, that every genuine row of the water-chemistry extract carries a `Startklok` value, and, with the recorded column list, that the CTD extract's readings carry a date and no clock time.
K-ENUMS.model: Each gzip extract is streamed through `csv.DictReader` with a semicolon delimiter and `latin-1` decoding. `rows` is incremented once for every record the reader yields, before any test. For each field, `nonblank[column]` is incremented when the column name is not `None` (so values spilling past the header are ignored), the value is not `None` (so a short record contributes nothing for the columns it lacks), and `value.strip()` is non-empty. The per-extract record is merged into the existing `enums.json`, replacing only that extract's key. The current `kemi` entry comes from the current code; the `ctd` entry carries no `nonblank` key, so it was written by an earlier version of the script and survives through the merge.
K-ENUMS.not_licensed: Anything about the water. These counts are not counts of samples, bottles, casts, stations or visits, since a record is one parameter reading. They say nothing about ODA's database beyond the fetched period and network. `Startklok` being present says nothing about whether the time is correct or which zone it is in. The gap between `kemi.rows` and `kemi.nonblank.Startklok` is not a count of samples without a clock.
K-ENUMS.title: Record and non-blank counts of the ODA extracts
void_if: An extract is re-fetched (a different period, station network or fetch date) and the script is not re-run for it: the entry then describes a file that is no longer on disk.

The script is changed to skip records with the wrong field count, or the source's quoting is repaired: `kemi.rows` would fall to `kemi.nonblank.Startklok`, and the apparent rows without a clock would disappear.
The file is read with a different delimiter, encoding or quoting rule than the one declared.
K-ENUMS.what: For every column of each named ODA extract, counts the distinct values (in full while the column looks categorical, as a reservoir-sampled numeric summary once it does not), the total number of records, and the number of records with a non-blank value in each column.

assumptions: The published sheets faithfully show the city's model for the design cloudburst on the city as it then stood.
Colour classification recovers the painted bands without admitting photographed roofs, water or shadow.

Each sheet is placed well enough that the water mask removes the painted harbour and lakes and not neighbouring land. The total is not placement-invariant, because both the water exclusion and the union of overlapping sheets depend on where each sheet sits.
Where sheets overlap they agree, so taking the deepest band per cell unions one flood, not two misplaced copies.
A grid cell counts as flooded whenever any sheet pixel inside it does, which is acceptable resampling even though partly flooded edge cells count whole.
The band below `FLOOD_DEPTH_MIN` is a wet film, not flooding.
The municipal and OSM water polygons mark open water correctly.

Every placement step omits the meridian convergence (`data/derived/convergence.json`). Its effect on this area, through the water mask and sheet overlaps, has never been computed; only its effect on the terrain check was tried.

`qa_flood_vs_water.passes` assumes that correctly placed flooding avoids open water. Part of the paint on water was placement error - it shrank when the sheets were registered against each other - and the rest may be the city's paint on lakes and the harbour, so neither PASS nor FAIL says anything about placement. No page renders it; it should be dropped, or replaced by a test resting on another premise, such as the bundle adjustment's residuals.

justified.text: Only sheets flagged as confidently registered are used.
Paint over lakes and harbour is excluded, since water standing on water is not something a cloudburst basin addresses, and is reported separately, not dropped.
The palette classification was tuned against named failure cases: white roofs matching the palest band, and a flatness test that erased real streaks.
The legend's swatches are blanked using positions from the PDF text layer, so they are not exported as fictional deep flooding.

The sheets were made mutually consistent by photograph-to-photograph matching and a bundle adjustment anchored on control points, and paint over open water fell, a quantity the adjustment did not optimise for.
How far the area moves when one sheet's placement changes is recorded on the site, not hidden.

K-FLOODGAP.licenses: How much ground the city's published cloudburst model paints at or above the threshold depth, within the area the recovered sheets cover, as read by this pipeline. It serves as the denominator for floodgap's statements about how much of that modelled flooding lies near planned or built works.
K-FLOODGAP.model: Each sheet's pixels have already been classified into depth bands by colour distance to the printed legend palette, with a blue-cast test for the palest band, a flatness test for the darker ones, and the legend itself blanked (`scripts/floodmaps.py:250`). floodgap.py builds a grid of `CELL` cells spanning every confident sheet, using fixed metres-per-degree constants `LATM` and `LONM`. It places each confident sheet north-up by its recorded north-west corner, scales pixels by the sheet's scale-bar `m_per_px`, truncates each pixel to a grid cell, and keeps the maximum band per cell across all pixels and sheets. Cells at or above `FLOOD_DEPTH_MIN` are flooded; cells under the rasterised water polygons (the municipal water layer, plus OSM water if that file is present) are removed. The area is the remaining cell count times the cell area.
K-FLOODGAP.not_licensed: That this area has flooded or will flood. It says nothing about the city as it is now: districts built since the model lie outside every sheet (`scripts/export_flood.py:68`), and the model has not been re-run on current terrain (`docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md:345`). It covers no flooding outside the sheets' footprint, gives no volume or depth beyond the band threshold, and is not precise to the digits printed, given resampling and sensitivity to placement.
K-FLOODGAP.title: Modelled flood area on land
void_if: Any sheet's registration changes. The area has moved with one sheet's placement before (`docs/KNOWN_AND_UNKNOWN.md:86`).

The band rasters are re-extracted with a different colour tolerance, flatness test or legend box.
The water polygons change, or the optional OSM water file appears or disappears.
The sheets are found to show a scenario or terrain other than the one they are described as showing.
K-FLOODGAP.what: Puts the depth bands recovered from the city's published flood-model sheets onto one metric grid, keeps the deepest band per cell, and counts the ground area modelled as flooded at or above a threshold depth, excluding open water. The result is the denominator of floodgap's coverage shares.

Flows are taken only from filings spanning roughly a year, and stock and flow come from the same filing.
Support services and property letting are excluded from primary agriculture by industry code, because they would drag every average.
The script labels the kg-N-to-animal-unit conversion as stated and not verified, and says declared parcels are not harmoniareal, so the line locates the threshold rather than testing it.
Landless holdings are counted as exposed because they have no base area of their own.

assumptions: The CVR number on a CHR herd row and the CVR number on a Marker parcel identify the same operating business, so a string match on CVR is a match of animals to the land that takes their manure.

Area declared for area support approximates the area a business can spread on. It is not harmoniareal: spreading agreements, rented spreading land and land declared by a partner company are all outside it.
The register's `DE` is a like-for-like measure of manure across species. The herd-size columns are not, which is why `DE` is used.
The two layers describe the same farms at compatible times, though they are different register years (`CHR24` for herds, `Marker_2025` for parcels).
The classic harmony line `harmony_1_4` is a meaningful marker of manure pressure, although it has no legal force.
CHR rows with a blank CVR hold herds that do not belong in the national total the page prints.
Values silently zeroed by `num()` are too few to matter.

gaps: Nothing in the repo justifies `harmony_1_4` as the land's physical capacity to take manure; it is a retired legal ceiling. The current binding ceiling is organic nitrogen per hectare of harmoniareal (source `BEK931-2024`, claim `C-DE-VOID`). At the nitrogen-per-animal-unit conversion that scripts/socialcontext.py states but says it has not verified, that ceiling corresponds to the `over_limit.[1.7]` line, not the `[1.4]` line. So the reading printed in NITROGEN.md, that the animals on those farms stand on declared land that cannot take their manure, and the `C-MANURE` note that 'the physical statement stands', claim more than the `[1.4]` line supports.

The claim text of `C-MANURE` in data/manual/claims.json calls `share_of_businesses_pct` a share 'of those declaring land'. The code's denominator is `cvrs_with_both` (businesses with `DE > 0` and `ha > 1`), a much smaller set than `cvrs_with_land`. The printed sentence misdescribes its own denominator, and NITROGEN.md's 'of those with land' is ambiguous in the same direction.

In `share_of_herd_pct` the numerator and denominator are counted under different rules. Businesses with animal units but no matched land fail `ha > 1` and are excluded from the numerator, although by the density rule they are above every line; their animal units stay in the denominator. How large a part of the CVR-registered herd these businesses hold is computed by no script. The printed share is therefore a floor on 'the herd on businesses whose own declared land is below the line', but it is printed as a share 'of the national herd' without that qualification.

`animal_units_total`, printed as the national herd, excludes CHR rows with a blank CVR. On the sibling's copy those rows are a large part of all rows and carry a small part of the animal units; no script here records either share. Neither the script nor the page mentions the exclusion.

`sites` is a row count, not a count of sites or locations. On the sibling's copy of `CHR24`, many CHR numbers carry several rows, and several rows share a CHR number and species. The sibling's data-sources doc says 'each feature is one site', the `D-CHR` node labels the count 'livestock sites', and NITROGEN.md prints it as 'Livestock sites'. Code and data disagree with those labels.
`num()` returns zero on any parse failure, the bare-except pattern the project's CLAUDE.md warns against. `formats.num()` is not used, and no count of zeroed values is recorded.
The `ha > 1` eligibility minimum is not explained in the script, its output or the page.
The pull stops at the first page shorter than requested and never checks the server's matched-feature count, although the sibling's fetchers do. A truncated page would silently shorten every total.

The output records no fetch date and no layer version. Recomputing from the sibling's fetched copies of the same layers reproduces `over_limit.[1.4].businesses` to within one business, not exactly, so the value depends on the live layer on the day of the fetch.
No reason is given for pairing a herd layer of one register year with a parcel layer of the next.
The script is not registered in data/manual/build.json. It reads no local file, only two live WFS layers, so the freshness check can never report its output stale.

justified.text: Both registers carry the operator's CVR number and the script joins on it; the layers and their traps were documented by the sibling project danish-livestock.
The sibling documents `DE` as the animal units under the manure regulation, and documents that the herd-size columns double-count for some species, which is the stated reason for using `DE`.
The server's false encoding declaration is handled by decoding as `latin-1`.

The sibling reports that the CHR cattle head count for the layer's year agrees closely with the Statistics Denmark census. That supports the register's coverage of cattle heads, though not its `DE` figures.
The threshold is declared stipulated and indicative, not a compliance test, in the script and in its output's `_stated` field.
The project's claim ledger pins the fertiliser regulation and finds the animal unit absent from its operative text, so the ledger qualifies every DE-per-hectare claim as indicative.
The eligibility rule and both denominators are exactly as described.
The page that prints these numbers discloses that declared area is not spreading area, that many animal-keeping businesses match no land, and that the thresholds are the old harmony units.

K-MANURE.licenses: Counts over the open registers: how many CVR-matched businesses have register animal units per declared hectare strictly above the classic harmony line, what fraction that is of businesses with both animals and land, and a lower bound on the share of the CVR-registered herd that stands on such businesses. Together these support a statement that declared area is small relative to the herd across a large part of the sector, at a stated and non-legal line.
K-MANURE.model: Two live WFS pulls from the agriculture ministry's GeoServer, attributes only, as CSV decoded as `latin-1`, a page at a time. CHR: every row is counted into `sites`; rows whose `CVRNR` is blank or `"0"` are then dropped, and `DE` is summed per CVR (`de_by_cvr`), whose sum is `animal_units_total`. Marker (`Marker_2025`): `IMK_areal` is summed per CVR (`ha_by_cvr`). A business enters the comparison only if `de_by_cvr[c] > 0` and `ha_by_cvr[c] > 1`; its density is $\mathrm{DE}/\mathrm{ha}$. For each line in `LIMITS`, `businesses` counts densities strictly above the line, `animal_units` sums those businesses' `DE`, $100\cdot\dfrac{\text{businesses}}{|\text{vals}|}$ (in the code `share_of_businesses_pct = 100 * businesses / len(vals)`) where `len(vals) == cvrs_with_both`, and $100\cdot\dfrac{\text{animal units}}{\text{animal units total}}$ (in the code `share_of_herd_pct = 100 * animal_units / animal_units_total`). Any `DE` or `IMK_areal` value that the script's own `num()` cannot parse is read as zero.
K-MANURE.not_licensed: Legal non-compliance; the claim that manure physically must leave these holdings (the line is a retired legal ceiling, not a measured capacity, and declared area is not spreading area); a share of all land-declaring businesses; the share of the whole herd on overstocked holdings (landless herds are excluded from the numerator); the number of livestock sites or farms; kilograms of manure nitrogen per hectare; anything about water quality directly.

void_if: A business's animals and its land are registered under different CVR numbers (holding company, partnership, spreading agreement). It then appears landless (excluded) or overstocked (counted) when it is neither.

The CHR or Marker layer has been revised since the fetch: the output carries no fetch date and would not show it.
The register's `DE` is defined differently from the old manure-regulation animal unit, or changes definition between layer years.
The count is read as a test of legal compliance. The animal unit has no legal force (`C-DE-VOID`).
`sites` is read as the number of livestock farms or distinct locations.
K-MANURE.what: Joins the livestock register (CHR, animal units per herd row) to the declared field-parcel register (Marker, hectares per parcel) on the operator's CVR number. For each business it divides animal units by declared hectares, then counts the businesses above each line in `LIMITS` and the animal units they hold.

assumptions: `Silicium` is reported as micrograms of the silicon element per litre, not as silicate or silicon dioxide. The code's comment asserts this for all parameters; it is not checked against a document.

Silicate, nitrite+nitrate and ammonium values in one cell refer to the same fraction (dissolved), although rows are not filtered on `Prøvefraktion` and the extract carries total, dissolved and particulate fractions.
A missing ammonium value means ammonium was negligible, not that it was unmeasured or below detection.
Dropping censored results does not bias the yearly median. Censoring removes exactly the cells where silicate or DIN is depleted, and in opposite directions for the two.

A median pooled over all seasons, stations and depths down to `10` metres represents the year's surface ratio, even though the stations sampled, the months sampled and the number of depths per station change from year to year.
Si:DIN, rather than Si to total nitrogen, is the ratio the hypothesis concerns.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read rescore.py after my edit: A5's still-missing list now names volume transport at the Belt and Sound sections, as A5's own Needs line asks and the source register finds no open series; the salinity key takes promille, the unit the extract carries; a docstring and a comment lost typed counts. The matrix logic and every test are unchanged - the tests read no salinity and select no hypothesis by class. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: Although the field sits under `tests`, it is not a test. There is no null, no uncertainty, and no control for station, season or depth, while the script's docstring promises only tests whose null is computable (`scripts/rescore.py:17-19`). The persistence-aware null worked out in `docs/hypodrafts/K1.md` is not applied.

The project's own `K1` design specifies the preceding January-February (pre-bloom) median surface Si:DIN as the quantity that matters, and warns that low silicon beside many diatoms is drawdown, not limitation (`docs/hypodrafts/K1.md`, under The observable consequence and Direction). This median pools all months, so it mixes pre-bloom pools with bloom drawdown.

Station composition changes across years, and the same draft notes that any across-year statistic on pooled medians is partly a statistic about who sampled (`docs/hypodrafts/K1.md`, under The null). Here there are no station fixed effects and no balanced panel.

Rows are not filtered on `Prøvefraktion`, and when a parameter has more than one row in a cell the last one read silently wins. A total and a dissolved silicate value, for example, are not distinguished.
Ammonium absent from a cell is treated as zero, which raises the ratio for that cell. Ammonium is reported on fewer rows than nitrite+nitrate (`counts.nh4.n` against `counts.nox.n`).
Silicate being reported as the element is asserted in a code comment, not documented.

Excluding censored values removes the low-silicate cells that are the very condition `K1` is about, and also the low-DIN cells. The net bias is unquantified and can drift as detection limits and DIN levels change.
Here `surface` means the top `10` metres, while `scripts/cycles.py` uses `MAX_DEPTH`. The same word names two different layers across the site.

The silicon-limitation threshold of one, used for the companion `share_below_1` and in the prose around these medians, rests on the unsourced statement in `docs/HYPOTHESES.md` (hypothesis `K2`) about the silicon-to-nitrogen ratio diatoms require.
The latest calendar year in the output is partial (the extract runs to its fetch date), so its median is taken over an unbalanced part of the season.

The draft keeps the policy-shock reading only as a conditional: if nitrogen fell under management and silicon has no human source, a rise in Si:DIN would be a change in the driver. Neither premise is established on the page, so a rise is not shown to be exogenous to diatoms.

justified.text: The hypothesis names the silicon-to-nitrogen ratio through time as one half of what discriminates it, and silicate as available in the ODA record.
The triage that blocked `K1` on this fetch states the hypothesis in terms of Si:DIN.
Parameter strings and units are taken from the enum sweep, and the unit is enforced per row, because several parameters appear under more than one unit.
Rows are dropped on unit, censoring, sample type, unparseable values and the depth sentinel before any cell is formed.
Censored rows are excluded because a detection limit read as a value biases the parameter high.
The ratio is molar, using element molar masses on concentrations reported as the element.
The ratio, the depth cut, the treatment of ammonium and the median index are exactly as described.

K-RESCORE.licenses: A descriptive statement about the archived bottle samples: in the top `10` metres, the pooled yearly median molar Si:DIN in this extract is higher in recent years than in the mid-eighties. That is a first look at the direction of `K1`'s driver, consistent with DIN having fallen while silicon did not.
K-RESCORE.model: Water-chemistry rows are kept when `Parameter` matches one of the exact strings in `P` with the unit `P` requires, `ResultatAttribut` is not `<` or `>`, the sample type is `Enkeltprøve` or `Blandingsprøve`, the result and depth parse, the date has `YYYYMMDD` form, and the depth is not the sentinel `99`. Each kept value is written into a dictionary keyed by station, date and depth rounded to one decimal; if a parameter appears more than once in a cell, the last row read wins. In `run_tests`, cells deeper than `10` metres, or lacking silicate or nitrite+nitrate, are skipped. DIN is `nox + (nh4 or 0.0)`, and cells where DIN or silicate is not positive are skipped. Each concentration in micrograms of element per litre is divided by that element's molar mass (`MM`) and the ratio is taken. Ratios are grouped by the year string, sorted, and the value at index `len(v) // 2` is reported, rounded, for each year with at least the minimum cell count.
K-RESCORE.not_licensed: Anything about diatoms, flagellates or community composition, which is the response half of `K1` and is not held. That the change is statistically established, monotonic, or true at any particular station or water body. That silicon limitation no longer occurs in any season, the pre-bloom winter pool in particular. That nitrogen management caused the rise. That the premise of `K1` is refuted as a mechanism rather than weakened as a trend.
K-RESCORE.title: Yearly median surface Si:DIN ratio
void_if: A year's cells are dominated by one season, a few stations or one area. This applies especially to the latest, partial year.
Some laboratories or periods report `Silicium` as silicate or silicon dioxide, or report a different fraction, under the same parameter string and unit.
Ammonium reporting or detection limits change over time enough to move which cells lose ammonium or are censored.
The extract is re-fetched, or `P`, the depth cut or the minimum cell count changes, and the script is not re-run.
K-RESCORE.what: After an availability matrix for the hypotheses that were blocked on the water-chemistry fetch, the script computes, for hypothesis `K1` (silicon depletion and the diatom-to-flagellate shift in `docs/HYPOTHESES.md`), the yearly distribution of the surface molar Si:DIN ratio: its median and its share below one. It computes only the nutrient driver; the phytoplankton-community response it is meant to drive is not held.

assumptions: Waves at each depth are those the local wind grows over the fetch in its direction; swell from outside the bay and currents are ignored.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read waves.py against agent w3-fr's findings: the claim that the threshold ratio is independent of calibration does not hold, so it is withdrawn and recorded as a gap, with the fetch table's ceiling; waves.py is unchanged. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

gaps: The critical stresses come from a comment citing the cohesive-sediment literature; no document is pinned.
No observation of sediment moving is used; the model is not checked against turbidity or sediment traps.
The fetch table it reads has no producer script in the repository.

The ratio of resuspending hours over the live and the dead threshold is not independent of the wave model's calibration: it depends on where the modelled shear distribution sits relative to both thresholds, so scaling the shear changes it. No sensitivity run has been done.

The fetch table's longest entries are the ray cast's ceiling, not distances to a coast: several south-easterly directions hold exactly the same maximum. Whether the cap matters for wave growth at the model depths has not been checked.

justified.text: Wave growth, dispersion and friction follow published relations written out in the script.

K-WATER-WAVES.licenses: How often, and in which months and winds, the wind could resuspend a live and a dead bed at the modelled depths, and how much more often the dead one.
K-WATER-WAVES.model: Fetch from the direction table; wave height and period from the shallow-water growth relations of Young and Verhagen (in the code `young_verhagen`); the wavenumber from the linear dispersion relation by iteration; bottom orbital velocity $u_b = \pi H_s / (T_p \sinh kd)$; shear $\tau = \tfrac{1}{2}\rho f_w u_b^2$ with the Swart friction factor (in the code `bed_shear`). A resuspending hour is one with $\tau$ above the bed's critical stress.
K-WATER-WAVES.not_licensed: That sediment actually moved in any given hour, or how much.
K-WATER-WAVES.title: Wind-driven waves and bed shear stress in Køge Bugt
void_if: waves in the bay are dominated by swell from outside it
the bed's critical stress differs strongly from the stated values across the bay
K-WATER-WAVES.what: Turns hourly wind into fetch-limited waves, bottom orbital velocity and bed shear stress at fixed depths, and counts the hours in which the shear exceeds the critical stress of a live and of a dead bed, by month and by wind sector.

field.is: For one calendar year (the `*` key, taken from the first four characters of `Startdato`), the median molar ratio $\dfrac{\mathrm{Si}/M_{\mathrm{Si}}}{(\mathrm{NO_x} + \mathrm{NH_4})/M_{\mathrm{N}}}$, with $M$ the molar masses (in the code `(si / MM["si"]) / ((nox + nh4) / MM["n"])`). It is taken over station-date-depth cells with depth `dep <= 10` metres that carry silicate (`Silicium`, `µg/l`) and nitrite+nitrate (`Nitrit+nitrat-N`, `µg/l`). Ammonium (`Ammoniak+ammonium-N`) is added when present and taken as zero when absent, and both silicate and DIN must be positive. The median is the element at index `len(v) // 2` of the sorted values, so for an even count it is the upper middle value. Censored results, depth-integrated samples, the depth sentinel `99` and wrong-unit rows are excluded, as are years with fewer cells than the script's minimum. One cell is one station, date and depth rounded to a decimetre, so a station's several shallow depths on one day are separate cells.

field.is: For one calendar year (the `*` key, taken from the first four characters of `Startdato`), the median molar ratio $\dfrac{\mathrm{Si}/M_{\mathrm{Si}}}{(\mathrm{NO_x} + \mathrm{NH_4})/M_{\mathrm{N}}}$, with $M$ the molar masses (in the code `(si / MM["si"]) / ((nox + nh4) / MM["n"])`). It is taken over station-date-depth cells with depth `dep <= 10` metres that carry silicate (`Silicium`, `µg/l`) and nitrite+nitrate (`Nitrit+nitrat-N`, `µg/l`). Ammonium (`Ammoniak+ammonium-N`) is added when present and taken as zero when absent, and both silicate and DIN must be positive. The median is the element at index `len(v) // 2` of the sorted values, so for an even count it is the upper middle value. Censored results, depth-integrated samples, the depth sentinel `99` and wrong-unit rows are excluded, as are years with fewer cells than the script's minimum. One cell is one station, date and depth rounded to a decimetre, so a station's several shallow depths on one day are separate cells.

field.is: A value as a document prints it, recorded with the exact phrase it sits in and the source it comes from. The field-surplus table entries are norm-product accounts from DCE SR120 Table 3.4, in kg N per hectare; the apportionment shares are percentages of land-based nitrogen to coastal waters. The G/M entries are chlorophyll-a boundaries in µg/l from the second opinion's `Tabel C.1` (the first scenario is VP3, the second the intercalibrated value); the Kd bins are the fractions of DCE's banding equation for Kd; the Hjarbæk entry is a percentage of the chlorophyll indicator.

One cell of NUAR Tabel 7.5: the change in gross margin (DB2, kroner per hectare) against the reference regulation, for one enterprise type in the Hjarbæk Fjord catchment, under one quota-allocation model; the last three models are the report's trading variants.

Ammonium (`Ammoniak+ammonium-N`) is added when present and taken as zero when absent, and both silicate and DIN must be positive. The median is the element at index `len(v) // 2` of the sorted values, so for an even count it is the upper middle value. Censored results, depth-integrated samples, the depth sentinel `99` and wrong-unit rows are excluded, as are years with fewer cells than the script's minimum. One cell is one station, date and depth rounded to a decimetre, so a station's several shallow depths on one day are separate cells.

code.text:
This is the part that surprises people, and it is the whole problem.

{B('C-LR-R-ERRORSADD')}Suppose the shop's delivery records are {Er()} out, its till records
are {Er()} out, and its physical count is {Er()} out, each independently of the others. You
might hope those wobbles cancel. In the residual they do not: independent errors add, in
variance, whatever their signs. The residual is a *difference between large numbers*. If
the shop turns over £{turn / 1e6:.0f}m and shrinkage is £{shr / 1e6:.0f}m, then a {Er()} error
in the £{turn / 1e6:.0f}m figure is £{e_gbp:,.0f} — {e_gbp / shr * 100:.0f}% of the answer. The
errors in each input are small **relative to that input**, and enormous **relative to the
leftovers**.{E}

code.text:
{B('C-LR-R-ERRORSADD')}Suppose the shop's delivery records are {Er()} out, its till records
are {Er()} out, and its physical count is {Er()} out, each independently of the others. You
might hope those wobbles cancel. In the residual they do not: independent errors add, in
variance, whatever their signs. The residual is a *difference between large numbers*. If
the shop turns over £{turn / 1e6:.0f}m and shrinkage is £{shr / 1e6:.0f}m, then a {Er()} error
in the £{turn / 1e6:.0f}m figure is £{e_gbp:,.0f} — {e_gbp / shr * 100:.0f}% of the answer. The
errors in each input are small **relative to that input**, and enormous **relative to the
leftovers**.{E}

kinds.bound: an inferred limit, not a value
kinds.calculated: arithmetic on other numbers, each with a kind of its own
kinds.computed: a deterministic consequence of stated inputs; no sampling error
kinds.counted: a number of things, under a stated rule of what counts as one
kinds.document: stated in a pinned external document
kinds.estimated: a statistic computed from measurements; it has sampling error
kinds.measured: an instrument or map reading, as recorded
kinds.modelled: the output of somebody's model of the world, not an observation of it
kinds.quoted: what this site said at an earlier commit
kinds.share: a part of something as a fraction of the whole
kinds.simulated: produced by a simulation; it can speak about the method, not the world
